text:
lina: quick q — thinking about splitting SIEM views so partner exports only get minimal fields (timestamp, tenant_id, event_type) to cut retention + kms complexity. any concerns for incident repro/forensics?

devon: sounds reasonable, need provenance though. if we strip user_agent/ip we lose triage signals. can we keep hashed identifiers? :thinking_face:

omar: agree with devon. hashed ip + original-ip encrypted and stored behind CMK with strict RBAC. export only the hash. on incident, JIT unwrap via ticket.

sara: +1 on JIT unwrap. question: who approves unwraps? we should avoid giving oncall blanket unwrap rights.

ben: proposal: retain full raw logs in cold storage for 180 days encrypted with CMK A, exportable views keep minimal fields for 30 days. unwrap requires 2-person approval + ticket id. that satisfies legal/forensics and reduces hot retention costs.

lina: dope. how do we handle SIEM alerts that reference fields we redact? e.g., suspicious-src-ip -> alert hits, but exported row won't show ip.

devon: keep alert payloads full inside internal SIEM only. partner-forwarded alerts get pointers (alert_id + minimal context). partner can request details via support flow.

audit-bot: export_job started by devops-service account for partner_acme at 2026-03-21T17:42:10Z.

omar: small technical nit — hashed identifiers must be salted per-tenant and rotateable. otherwise cross-tenant correlation possible.

sara: +1. add rotation policy: salt rotate every 90d, re-hash backfilled records with new salt into a rotation table (not in exports).

ben: example policy snippet we can put in docs: ```json
{"export_policy":"minimal", "fields":["ts","tenant_id","event_type","tenant_hash_ip"], "retention_days":30, "unwrap_path":"/security/jit-unwrap" }
```

lina: love that. who owns the CMK configuration (key rotation, grants) for partner unwraps? infra or secops?

omar: infra owns CMKs but secops owns unwrap workflow/approvals. infra provides KMS logs + key usage alerts.

devon: also point — RBAC boundary: create a scoped role 'siem_unwrap_approver' that can grant tickets for unwrap, requires SSO MFA and 90d re-approval.

sara: can we automate teardown of temporary access? e.g., unwrap creates a 1hr temporary read grant to artifact store. logs recorded to forensic bucket.

ben: yes — ephemeral access via short-lived creds is standard. add audit trail: who unwrapped, ticket id, reason, TTL. store that in immutable audit log (retention 7y).

lina: ok next steps: 1) devon/omar draft exported-field whitelist + hashing scheme, 2) infra/ben draft CMK ownership + rotation SOP, 3) sara draft unwrap approval flow w/ ticket template. i'll sync with legal on retention windows.

devon: i'll start PR with field whitelist and sample query for export filter.

omar: i'll write the KMS grant diagram and ephemeral creds flow.

sara: i'll write the approval playbook and add escalation matrix.

lina: awesome thanks. tagging @oncall-notify in case anyone needs to block exports in the meantime.

audit-bot: policy_change_detected: export_policy minimal proposed by devon. review url: https://redwood.internal/policies/siem-minimal-exports/6001239999

ben: fyi — add metric: percent of export rows with hashed_ip present vs full_ip to verify masking coverage.

lina: good call. will add to dashboard.

sara: can we also add an incident playbook appendix that says when to bypass minimal export (e.g., court order)? i'll coord with legal.

lina: perfect. ok closing thread, will update the RFC draft when PRs land. :white_check_mark:
